name: webdata-tools-mcp
description: Twenty-seven web-data tools for agents: jobs, hiring signals, news, public tenders, new laws and bills, Indian district notices, grants and funding calls, government updates, weather and disaster alerts, research papers and patents, field trends and idea validation, reviews, Reddit leads, contacts, real estate, Shopify, exhibitors, events.
long_description: Runs ready-made Apify Actors (published by tacps126) on your own Apify account and returns clean JSON. Covers job postings from career pages, remote-job feeds, Dice, Indeed and Naukri, hiring signals, Google News, official government updates (US Federal Register, GOV.UK, European Commission, SEC, RBI, SEBI), public tenders and contract awards (US SAM.gov, EU TED, UK, France, Spain, Germany, Netherlands, Canada, Colombia, Australia, South Africa), research papers, preprints and patents, technology-field landscapes and idea validation, Trustpilot and app-store reviews, Reddit mentions, YouTube transcripts, sanctions screening, product recalls, company registers, website contact details, German property listings, Shopify products and store analysis, trade-show exhibitor lists and upcoming events. Two analyst prompts (field-opportunity-analysis, idea-validation) turn the research tools into a model-agnostic innovation analyst. You pay Apify per result (about $1-3 per 1,000); every call has a spend cap.

tools.name: search_google_news
tools.description: Search Google News (any language and country) and return articles with the publisher's real article URL, publisher, date and related coverage. Supports Google operators ("exact phrase", -exclude, OR, intitle:) and site filters.

tools.name: find_hiring_companies
tools.description: Buying-intent signal: which companies are hiring for the roles you care about, how many roles, how fresh, and seniority/locations. Give target accounts (their jobs-page URLs on Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday, SmartRecruiters, Recruitee, Personio, Teamtailor) and/or job-search phrases to discover companies.

tools.name: get_company_jobs
tools.description: All open jobs from companies in one normalized format (title, company, location with country code, remote/hybrid, seniority, salary, skills, apply URL, posted date). Give career-page URLs (the company's own careers page or its job board) or just company names; 13 job-board systems are supported (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday, SmartRecruiters, Workable, Rippling, BambooHR, Pinpoint, Breezy, Recruitee, Personio, Teamtailor) and found automatically.

tools.name: find_remote_jobs
tools.description: Remote jobs straight from employers: hundreds of company job boards plus the Remote OK, Jobicy, Working Nomads and Himalayas feeds, keeping only roles the posting marks as remote. Normalized title, company, country, seniority, salary and skills; each job links to its source.

tools.name: search_startup_jobs
tools.description: Startup jobs from Wellfound by role and city, or remote: title, startup name, size and pitch, salary and equity range, years of experience, remote or on-site, apply link.

tools.name: search_tech_jobs
tools.description: US tech jobs from Dice by keyword and city: title, company, location, salary text, employer type (direct hire or recruiter), Easy Apply, remote / on-site / hybrid, posted and updated dates.

tools.name: search_indeed_jobs
tools.description: Search Indeed job listings by keyword and location in 9 countries (us, uk, ca, au, ie, de, fr, nl, sg): title, company, location, salary, job type, benefits, skills, apply link and (with details) the full job description.

tools.name: search_naukri_jobs
tools.description: Jobs from Naukri.com, India's largest job board, by keyword and city: title, company, AmbitionBox rating, experience range in years, skills, and (with details) the full description, salary in rupees, industry, department and qualifications.

tools.name: get_trustpilot_reviews
tools.description: Trustpilot reviews for one or more companies (rating, title, text, reviewer, country, date, company reply) plus the company's TrustScore and review counts. Filter by stars, language, verified and date period.

tools.name: get_app_reviews
tools.description: Reviews from the Apple App Store and Google Play in one dataset: rating, text, author, date, app version, developer reply, sentiment. Mix both stores and several countries.

tools.name: search_reddit
tools.description: Reddit posts (and optionally comments) by keyword, subreddit or user: title, text, author, subreddit, score, links and dates. Good for brand and topic monitoring.

tools.name: find_reddit_leads
tools.description: Reddit posts and comments where people ask for a tool like yours, look for an alternative to a competitor, compare options or complain. Each lead is tagged with its intent (recommendation_request, alternative_seeking, comparison, pain_point) and the phrase that showed it.

tools.name: search_research
tools.description: Papers, preprints and patents from OpenAlex, arXiv, PubMed and Europe PMC in one deduplicated list, newest first or most influential first: title, abstract, authors and affiliations, venue, DOI, PDF link, citations, citations per year, field-normalized impact (top 1% / 10%), open-access status, and for patents the number, applicants and IPC/CPC classes. Retracted papers are left out.

tools.name: search_gov_updates
tools.description: Official government updates in one list: US Federal Register rules, proposed rules (with comment deadlines) and notices, SEC press releases, GOV.UK news, guidance and consultations, European Commission press releases, Indian regulators (RBI, SEBI, TRAI, CERC, CDSCO, DGFT) circulars, orders and notifications, plus any RSS feed or official "What's new" list page you name. Filter by sector, keyword, authority and type; every update is tagged with its sectors.

tools.name: get_alerts
tools.description: Official warnings in force from national services in one schema: US National Weather Service, MeteoAlarm (38 European countries), India NDMA (IMD, CWC, state disaster authorities), Brazil INMET, plus worldwide GDACS disasters and USGS earthquakes. Event, hazard type, severity, areas, start and expiry, instructions, issuing service. Most severe first.

tools.name: search_grants
tools.description: Open and forecast public funding calls in one schema: US Grants.gov (every federal agency), EU Funding & Tenders (Horizon Europe, Digital Europe, LIFE, EU4Health, Erasmus+, cascade calls) and UKRI. Title, funder, programme, grant size (min/max), total budget, expected awards, deadline, eligibility, contacts, link. Soonest deadline first.

tools.name: get_india_district_notices
tools.description: Tenders, recruitment and announcements from the official websites of India's 748 districts (collector offices), by state and district: title (often Hindi or the state language), date, district, state, official PDF link. Newest first.

tools.name: search_legislation
tools.description: New legislation from official publishers in one schema: EU regulations, directives and decisions (EUR-Lex), UK Acts and statutory instruments of all four nations (legislation.gov.uk), US public laws and bill texts with their stage (GovInfo), Australian Acts and legislative instruments (Federal Register of Legislation), Canadian regulations (Canada Gazette Part II). Number, title, date, sectors, official text and PDF links. Newest first.

tools.name: screen_sanctions
tools.description: Screens people and organisations against the official sanctions lists read from each publisher: US OFAC SDN and consolidated (non-SDN), UN Security Council, EU consolidated financial sanctions, UK Sanctions List and Canada. Matching handles transliteration (Cyrillic, Arabic), word order, patronymics, initials and company forms. Returns a verdict per name (match, possible-match, no-match) with the matching entries: list, programmes, countries, birth dates, identifiers, listing date and link. A screening aid, not legal advice.

tools.name: search_recalls
tools.description: Product recalls and safety alerts from regulators in one schema: US FDA enforcement reports (food, drugs, medical devices), US CPSC consumer products, Health Canada / CFIA / Transport Canada, UK Food Standards Agency and OPSS, and the EU Safety Gate. Product, brands, company, hazard, class, date, distribution, remedy and official link. Newest first.

tools.name: find_companies
tools.description: Official company registers in one schema. mode "new": companies newly registered in France (BODACC), Norway (Brønnøysund) and Finland (PRH), and in France also insolvency judgments, deregistrations and business sales; filter by NACE/NAF industry code, city/region/postcode and keywords. mode "search": companies by name in France (with officers), Norway, Finland and, for other countries, the worldwide LEI index. Registry id, legal form, status, dates, industry, address, employees, capital, officers, register link.

tools.name: get_supplier_contracts
tools.description: Public contracts each company won: US federal (USAspending), every EU/EEA country (TED award notices) and the UK (Contracts Finder). First a summary per company (awards, total value per currency, top buyers, first and last award, legal names the portals used), then every award with buyer, value, date, codes and link. For competitor tracking, sales prospecting and supplier due diligence.

tools.name: search_tenders
tools.description: Public procurement notices from official portals in one schema: US SAM.gov (federal), EU TED (every EU/EEA country), UK Find a Tender and Contracts Finder, France BOAMP, Spain PLACSP, Germany, Netherlands TenderNed, Canada CanadaBuys, Colombia SECOP II, Brazil PNCP, India GeM, Ukraine Prozorro, EU institutions (Funding & Tenders portal), US contract awards (USAspending), Australia AusTender (awards) and South Africa eTenders. Title, buyer, deadline, value and currency, CPV/UNSPSC/NAICS codes, sectors, buyer contacts, suppliers for awards, notice link. Open tenders by default.

tools.name: analyze_field
tools.description: A landscape of a technology or research field from open research data: an opportunity score (0-100) with its reasons, momentum, lab-to-market gap and geographic concentration; works per year and growth stage; industry participation and the top companies; key researchers, institutions, countries and funders; rising sub-topics, standout recent work and related patents. Several fields come back ranked. For written opportunities, use the field-opportunity-analysis prompt.

tools.name: validate_idea
tools.description: How much research already covers a product or research idea: matching works, works in the last two years, crowdedness (open, early, active, crowded), growth, who is working on it (researchers, institutions, companies), the closest prior work and related patents. For a written assessment, use the idea-validation prompt.

tools.name: find_website_contacts
tools.description: Finds business emails, phone numbers, addresses and social profiles (LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube) on any list of websites; it visits the contact and about pages itself. Use only for lawful business outreach (GDPR / CAN-SPAM).

tools.name: search_german_property_listings
tools.description: Apartments and houses for rent or sale in Germany or Austria: price, rent, area, rooms, address with coordinates, energy class, features, agent, photos and dates. Not Switzerland.

tools.name: get_shopify_products
tools.description: Products from any Shopify store: prices, sale prices, discounts, stock, variants, SKUs, images and descriptions. Whole stores, collections or single products. Useful for price and stock monitoring.

tools.name: analyze_shopify_stores
tools.description: For each Shopify store: name, city and country, currency, product and collection counts, a catalog snapshot (price range and median, share on sale and in stock, top brands and product types, newest product) and its e-mails, phones and social profiles. Non-Shopify sites are skipped for free.

tools.name: get_trade_show_exhibitors
tools.description: Exhibitor lists of trade shows as B2B leads: company, booth and hall, email, phone, website, address, socials and categories. 91 built-in shows (e.g. medica, sema-show, nab-show, fabtech, ish, automechanika, wtm-london, orgatec, eurotier, wine-paris, biofach) or any exhibitor-list link or show homepage on Messe Frankfurt, Messe Düsseldorf, Koelnmesse, NürnbergMesse, Newfront/ExpoPlatform, RX, Map Your Show, a2z / A2Z Connect, Swapcard or Corussoft; the link's own show and year are used. Contact coverage depends on what the organiser publishes.

tools.name: find_events
tools.description: Upcoming events by topic and city, or from Luma / Eventbrite / Meetup links (or any page with schema.org events): name, dates, venue with address and coordinates, organiser, hosts, ticket prices, free/sold-out and attendee count, in one format. Use for event prospecting, sponsorships and community research.

prompts.name: field-opportunity-analysis
prompts.description: Analyse one or more technology or research fields with analyze_field, then write ranked, evidence-backed product and business opportunities (why now, capital needed, who to talk to).
prompts.text:
Call the analyze_field tool with fields ${arguments.fields} (one call for all of them; several fields come back ranked by opportunity score).
Then use only its records as the evidence.
The analysis is for ${arguments.audience}.

You are a pragmatic technology and innovation analyst advising founders, R&D leaders and investors.
From the field evidence, find concrete product or business opportunities.
For each opportunity say what to build, for whom, why now (which signal shows the timing), what it would take
(capital bucket: under $50k software/service, $50k-$1M hardware or regulated software, over $1M deep tech, manufacturing or clinical),
and who in the evidence could be a partner, customer or competitor.
Be specific, cite the signals you rely on, and say when the evidence is thin. No generic advice.

How to read the evidence:
- scores.opportunity (0-100) and scores.why: the overall ranking and the signals behind it.
- scores.momentum (0-100): research output in the last two full years against the two before; 50 = about +40%.
- scores.labToMarketGap (0-100): high momentum with few company authors — research is ahead of products.
- industry.recentShare: share of recent works with a company author (under 5% academic, 5-15% engaging, over 15% active); industry.trend says whether companies are moving in or out.
- scores.geographicConcentration: share of the top country among the leading countries; high means one country dominates (supply-chain, policy and partner risk).
- risingTopics: sub-topics whose share grew most; standoutRecentWorks: the most cited recent papers.
- topCompanies / keyResearchers / topInstitutions / topFunders: who to partner with, hire from, license from or compete against.
- reviewShare: a high share of review papers means the field is consolidating.
- broaderSpace / position (validation): the biggest neighbouring space with one term left out; "open niche in a crowded field" means the application is new but the technology around it is busy (competition for talent, suppliers and attention; also proof the base technology works).
- relatedPatents.likelyExpiredByTerm: filed more than 20 years ago — possibly free to use (not legal advice).
Small counts make percentages noisy — say so when growth.stage reports it.

Answer in these sections:
1. Summary — two or three sentences; when several fields were analysed, the ranking and why.
2. Opportunities — three to five, best first. For each: the idea, for whom, why now, capital bucket with the reason, who to talk to.
3. Risks.
4. Evidence quality — strong, moderate or thin, and why.

prompts.name: idea-validation
prompts.description: Check an idea with validate_idea (how much research already covers it, who is working on it, closest prior work, related patents), then assess novelty, timing, capital, risks and next steps.
prompts.text:
Call the validate_idea tool with ideas ["${arguments.idea}"].
Then use only its record as the evidence. If the idea is broad, you may also call analyze_field on its core technology for growth and industry signals.

You are a pragmatic technology and innovation analyst. Assess the idea against the evidence:
how new it is (crowdedness, closest prior work), whether the timing is right (growth), who is already working on it
(researchers, institutions, companies), what it would take to build (capital bucket: under $50k, $50k-$1M, over $1M),
the main risks, and the three most useful next steps. Be specific, cite the evidence, and say when it is thin.

How to read the evidence:
- scores.opportunity (0-100) and scores.why: the overall ranking and the signals behind it.
- scores.momentum (0-100): research output in the last two full years against the two before; 50 = about +40%.
- scores.labToMarketGap (0-100): high momentum with few company authors — research is ahead of products.
- industry.recentShare: share of recent works with a company author (under 5% academic, 5-15% engaging, over 15% active); industry.trend says whether companies are moving in or out.
- scores.geographicConcentration: share of the top country among the leading countries; high means one country dominates (supply-chain, policy and partner risk).
- risingTopics: sub-topics whose share grew most; standoutRecentWorks: the most cited recent papers.
- topCompanies / keyResearchers / topInstitutions / topFunders: who to partner with, hire from, license from or compete against.
- reviewShare: a high share of review papers means the field is consolidating.
- broaderSpace / position (validation): the biggest neighbouring space with one term left out; "open niche in a crowded field" means the application is new but the technology around it is busy (competition for talent, suppliers and attention; also proof the base technology works).
- relatedPatents.likelyExpiredByTerm: filed more than 20 years ago — possibly free to use (not legal advice).
Small counts make percentages noisy — say so when growth.stage reports it.

Answer in these sections: Novelty, Closest prior work, Timing, Who is already there,
Capital (bucket and why), Risks, Next steps (three), Evidence quality (strong, moderate or thin).

apify_token.title: Apify API token
apify_token.description: From Apify Console > Settings > API & Integrations. Actors run on your account.

max_charge_usd.title: Maximum spend per tool call (USD)
max_charge_usd.description: Apify stops a run when this is reached.

timeout_secs.title: Maximum wait per tool call (seconds)
timeout_secs.description: How long one call may run before it is stopped (30 to 300).
